title: Senior Returns Manager, EU
description:
ABOUT QUINCE

Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes  and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.

What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.

OUR CULTURE

Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.

  • We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA.  Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
  • Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths. 
  • Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory. 

If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.

About the Role

We're looking for a Returns Manager to own end-to-end reverse logistics performance across our UK and EU operations. From forecasting incoming volume through grading, refunds, fraud prevention, and resale, you'll build a returns operation that's fast, accurate, and cost-efficient — while turning returned inventory back into recovered value. This is a hands-on role for someone who can dig into root causes, manage partners and carriers, and build the reporting to prove it's working.

What You'll Do

Returns Forecasting & Planning

  • Build and maintain returns volume forecasting models across UK and EU markets, factoring in seasonality, backlog, promotions, and category-level return patterns
  • Translate forecasts into staffing, processing capacity, and warehouse space plans for returns operations
  • Monitor returns rate trends and flag volume shifts to inventory, finance, and merchandising teams

 

Customer Refunds

  • Oversee timely, accurate refund processing in line with UK and EU consumer rights regulations
  • Audit warehouse/QRC staff on grading standards and quality checks
  • Partner with customer service and finance to resolve refund discrepancies and disputes
  • Track refund turnaround time against SLA and resolve bottlenecks in the refund workflow

 

Fraud Detection & Prevention

  • Build and refine fraud detection processes for returns abuse (wardrobing, serial returners, empty-box claims, item-not-as-described fraud)
  • Partner with risk and customer service teams to develop fraud rules/flags and investigate high-risk cases
  • Balance fraud prevention with customer experience, avoiding over-blocking of legitimate returns

 

Returns Root Cause & Logistics Feedback

  • Track and categorize return reasons, with particular focus on logistics-driven returns (damaged in transit, wrong item shipped, late or failed delivery, packaging failure)
  • Partner with warehouse, supply chain, and carrier teams to reduce logistics-driven returns through root cause analysis and corrective action
  • Present return reason trends to leadership to inform packaging, product, and logistics improvements

 

Returns Resale & Recommerce

  • Manage resale/recommerce channels for graded inventory (open-box, refurbished, clearance, secondary market and liquidation partners)
  • Maximize recovery value on returned inventory while minimizing time-to-resale
  • Build and manage relationships with resale/liquidation partners and evaluate new recommerce channels across UK and EU markets

 

Reverse Logistics & Carrier Management

  • Negotiate rates and service levels with carriers for return shipments across UK and EU markets
  • Manage carrier performance for return pickups, label generation, and inbound transit times
  • Evaluate and roll out returns-specific shipping options (paperless returns, drop-off points, pickup services) to reduce cost and improve the customer experience

 

SLA & Performance Management

  • Define and manage SLAs across the returns lifecycle — receipt to grading, grading to disposition, refund turnaround, and time-to-resale
  • Monitor 3PL and warehouse partner performance against returns SLAs; escalate and resolve issues as needed
  • Build reporting and dashboards to track returns KPIs and turn data into actionable recommendations for leadership

 

Cross-Functional & Compliance

  • Partner with customer service, supply chain, finance, and merchandising to align returns operations with broader business goals
  • Ensure returns operations comply with UK and EU consumer protection, distance selling, and VAT/duty rules (including treatment of re-imported goods and refund-related VAT adjustments)
  • Stay current on evolving returns-related regulation across UK and EU markets

What You'll Bring

Required

  • 5–8+ years managing returns or reverse logistics operations in a high-volume ecommerce or retail environment, ideally across UK and EU markets
  • Experience building returns forecasting and capacity planning models
  • Solid understanding of UK and EU consumer rights, refund, and distance-selling regulations
  • Experience designing or managing returns fraud detection and prevention programs
  • Track record reducing logistics-driven returns through root cause analysis and cross-functional fixes
  • Experience managing return resale, refurbishment, or liquidation channels
  • Carrier negotiation experience for reverse logistics/return shipping
  • Strong SLA and KPI management skills, with reporting experience (Excel, SQL, or BI tools)
  • Hands-on experience with WMS/OMS returns modules
  • Excellent cross-functional communication and stakeholder management skills

 

Preferred

  • Experience in DTC, fashion/apparel, or other high-return-rate ecommerce categories
  • Familiarity with recommerce or liquidation platforms and partners
  • Experience operating across multiple EU countries and languages
  • Background in fraud/risk analytics
  • Experience managing reverse logistics SLAs with UK/EU carriers (e.g., Royal Mail, Evri, DPD, DHL, GLS)

Joining Quince means being part of a mission-driven team reshaping retail. You will work alongside talented colleagues, tackle meaningful challenges, and contribute to building a more sustainable, accessible future for customers and partners alike.

title: Senior Software Engineer, .Net
description: Who We Are NeuroFlow CEO and West Point graduate Christopher Molaro served in the army for five years, including a tour in Iraq as a platoon leader. Coming back home, he experienced firsthand the gaps in the behavioral health system and how veterans and civilians alike face too many barriers when it comes to receiving appropriate, timely care. While pursuing his MBA at Wharton, Chris met his future co-founder Adam Pardes, and the two agreed – even the most engaging digital mental health apps in the world wouldn’t truly change the problem; only a solution that systematically integrated behavioral health into the full healthcare ecosystem could create meaningful change. And so they created NeuroFlow. What We Do We pride ourselves on partnering with healthcare leaders to assist in driving better outcomes, lowering total cost of care, and making behavioral health risk more predictable and transparent. NeuroFlow exists to make sure no one who needs behavioral health support falls through the cracks. We build more than just engaging digital health tools for self-care: we create platforms that identify population behavioral health risk early, engage individuals with acuity-specific resources, and enable care teams to make smarter and more efficient decisions. Together, NeuroFlow’s solutions arm healthcare organizations with the insights they need to overcome the systemic challenges in today’s healthcare ecosystem. How We Do It The award-winning culture at NeuroFlow is one built around encouragement and daring to be great. Our core values have been displayed in our office since day one, and each team member is responsible for carrying out these values and keeping each other accountable to them. We succeed through our flexibility and agility, navigating and transforming an industry ripe for change where “no” or “can’t” is too often the default. NeuroFlow offers unique opportunities to work in a fun and challenging fast-paced environment with direct, meaningful impact on helping to close the divide between mental and physical health. NeuroFlow is backed by investors including HLM Venture Partners, SEMCAP Health, Concord Health Partners, Builders VC, and Dreamit, alongside grant funding from the National Science Foundation and the U.S. Department of Defense. Our work has been recognized by TIME Magazine as one of the World's Top HealthTech Companies of 2025, by Fierce Healthcare's 2026 Fierce15, and by MedTech Breakthrough's Best Overall Mental Health Solution award. About the Role As a Senior Software Engineer at NeuroFlow, you build and maintain the full-stack features behind our behavioral health technology. Your team sets the goals and explains why they matter. From there, you work out what to build and how to build it, own the services in your team's domain, and help newer engineers grow along the way. What You'll Do Turn team goals into technical plans, then design and build full-stack features and services within your team's domain. Choose the methods, tools, and evaluation criteria for your own work, and walk your team through the tradeoffs. Spot technical risks and blockers early and propose fixes before they slow down delivery. Own the prioritization of your assigned work and bring it to your manager for approval. Contribute to architecture and design discussions for your team's services. Work with product, QA, and adjacent engineering teams to ship features in your team's domain. Mentor junior engineers through code review, pairing, and hands-on technical guidance. Improve testing, tooling, and engineering practices on the services you own. What You Should Have Typically 5+ years of professional experience in full-stack web development. Strong object-oriented programming skills in C#, solid TypeScript, and hands-on experience with .NET Framework or .NET 5+. Proficiency with a modern front-end framework such as Angular, React, or Vue. Experience building backend APIs and services with .NET Framework or .NET 5+. Working experience with ORMs and relational databases (for example, nHibernate, Entity Framework, SQL Server). Experience writing unit, integration, and UI automation tests. Experience with CI/CD tooling such as GitHub Actions or Azure DevOps. Experience with Docker and Kubernetes, whether running them in production or helping a team migrate to them. Nice to have Experience with cloud architectures on AWS or Azure. Familiarity with healthcare interoperability standards such as HL7 and FHIR. Experience building integrations with EHRs. Who You Are An engineer who owns your work from design through production and enjoys helping newer engineers level up. A clear communicator who can explain a technical decision to your team and stay open to other approaches. Someone who gets satisfaction from taking a tangled piece of code and making it simpler to maintain. Selected candidates will be subject to a government security investigation and must meet all eligibility requirements. NeuroFlow will support the clearance process. Obtaining clearance is required to remain in this position. Every day we are working to tackle the mental health crisis in America, and in order to do that well, we need diverse voices, experiences, and perspectives at the table. As an equal opportunity employer, we prohibit any unlawful discrimination against a job applicant on the basis of their race, color, religion, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, national origin, family or parental status, disability*, age, veteran status, or any other status protected by the laws or regulations in the locations where we operate. We respect the laws enforced by the EEOC and are dedicated to going above and beyond in fostering diversity across our workplace. *Applicants with disabilities may be entitled to reasonable accommodation under the terms of the Americans with Disabilities Act and certain state or local laws. A reasonable accommodation is a change in the way things are typically done which will ensure an equal employment opportunity without imposing undue hardship on NeuroFlow.
